patterns.rationale: AWS access key IDs follow an exact 20-character format (4-char prefix + 16 uppercase alphanumeric). Both Miss 1 (AKIA5RHE7Q2VFXJ4LWMK) and Miss 5 (AKIAQR7N3K2VPLMX9JFC) embed real-format AKIDs. Legitimate documentation uses redacted placeholders, never this exact format.
patterns.fp_notes: AWS SDK docs and tutorials sometimes show example keys, but always as clearly fake/placeholder strings — the exact 16-char uppercase-alphanumeric body is highly distinctive.

patterns.rationale: Covers the remaining service-token formats across the five misses: GitHub PAT (ghp_, Miss 1), HashiCorp Vault service token (hvs., Miss 2), Anthropic admin key (sk-ant-admin, Miss 3), OpenAI project key (sk-proj-, Miss 3), GitLab runner token (glrt-, Miss 4), Slack bot token (xoxb-, Miss 4), npm automation token (npm_, Miss 5). Minimum-length suffixes are set above the longest common legitimate env-var name to suppress noise (e.g., npm_config_* variables are far shorter than 30 chars).
patterns.fp_notes: sk-proj- could appear in OpenAI integration guides, but the 20-char suffix requirement filters placeholder values. npm_config_cache, npm_lifecycle_event etc. are well below the 30-char threshold. The known-good corpus contains none of these token formats.

patterns.rationale: Miss 3 embeds an explicit exfil destination under the key forward_target, disguised as a cache-entry attribute. This is semantically equivalent to send.*to.*http but uses a neutral attribute name to evade the existing exfil patterns. The combination of this specific key name with an HTTP(S) URL is unambiguous.
patterns.fp_notes: "forward_target" is not a standard attribute name in any observability, caching, or config framework. No known-good corpus file uses it.

patterns.rationale: All five misses share a "prior system already collected this legitimately, just process/emit it" framing — which is a false-authorization pattern fitting the FAKE_AUTH axis. Each miss uses a distinct phrase: "previously hydrated" (Miss 3 cache framing), "prior span emitted" (Miss 1 OTEL framing), "snapshot recorded by prior assertion" (Miss 4 test framing), "replay required for parity" (Miss 4), "checkpoint…stage-N-complete" (Miss 2 Step Functions framing), "previous job in this workflow completed" (Miss 5 GitHub Actions framing). These phrases claim an antecedent authority that pre-authorized the credential data, bypassing all override-language axes.
patterns.fp_notes: "stage-\d+-complete" alone could appear in CI docs, but the required "checkpoint" prefix tightens it. "previously hydrated" and "prior span emitted" are not natural phrases in legitimate documentation. The known-good corpus (deployment checklist, incident playbook, security policy, API reference) contains none of these constructions.

semantic_note: All five misses embed credential tokens with format-specific prefixes (AKIA, ghp_, glrt-, xoxb-, npm_, hvs., sk-ant-admin-) that are regex-catchable. The behavioral framing is also phrase-specific enough for narrow regex.
